title: Symmetric Tree
spaceBreakdown:
- recursion call-stack depth: O(h), worst case O(n) for a skewed tree, O(log n) for balanced
- no containers/arrays allocated
- not counted: input tree
approach: A tree is symmetric if its left and right subtrees are mirrors of each other. Two subtrees are mirrors when their root values are equal, the left child of one mirrors the right child of the other, and the right child of one mirrors the left child of the other. We implement this as a recursive helper `isMirror(a, b)` that checks both-null (true), one-null (false), value mismatch (false), then recurses in a crossed fashion: `isMirror(a->left, b->right) && isMirror(a->right, b->left)`.
hints: If you compare the root's left and right subtrees, what must be true about their children for the whole tree to fold in half along its center? The tree has at most 1000 nodes.

Use a recursive helper `isMirror(a, b)` checking two nodes are mirrors: values equal, `a.left` mirrors `b.right`, `a.right` mirrors `b.left`. In Example 1, `isMirror(node 2, node 2)` recurses into pairs (3,3) and (4,4), all matching.

```
isMirror(a, b):
    if both null: return true
    if one null: return false
    if a.val ≠ b.val: return false
    return isMirror(a.left, b.right) and isMirror(a.right, b.left)

isSymmetric(root):
    return isMirror(root.left, root.right)
```

**Single node** - only the root exists, both children are null
`Input: [1]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: returning false when both nodes are null instead of true → returns `false`

**Skewed tree** - left child exists, right child is null
`Input: [1,2,null]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking `a->val == b->val` before null-checking → dereferences null, crashes

**All-equal values, asymmetric structure** - every node value is 2 but positions differ
`Input: [1,2,2,2,null,2,null]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: only comparing values `return a->val == b->val` without recursing on children → returns `true`

**Crossed children** - must compare left.left with right.right, not left.left with right.left
`Input: [1,2,2,3,4,4,3]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: recursing `isMirror(a.left, b.left)` instead of `isMirror(a.left, b.right)` → returns `false`

followUps.q: Can you solve this iteratively without recursion?
followUps.a: Use a queue of node pairs. Enqueue (root.left, root.right), then for each pair: if both null continue, if one null return false, if values differ return false, else enqueue (a.left, b.right) and (a.right, b.left). TC O(n), SC O(n).

followUps.q: What if the tree has 10^7 nodes and recursion depth is a concern?
followUps.a: The recursive approach uses O(h) call-stack space which can overflow on a skewed tree. Switch to the iterative queue approach which allocates on the heap instead. TC O(n), SC O(n).

followUps.q: Check whether any subtree of the given tree is symmetric.
followUps.a: Run the mirror check at every node treating it as a root. Naively this is O(n²) since each check is O(n) and there are n nodes. TC O(n²), SC O(h) for the recursion at each node.
